rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 1 (score 134.06, kp 3.0, kd 0.4, 12 mm sensors at x = ±0.03) is still the best raced design. Iteration 4 (score 122.26) widened the array to ±0.04 with 16 mm footprints, raised kp to 3.7 and kd to 0.5, and scored lower. Its oval score rose to 235 because of one completion, but its s-bend progress fell slightly (0.245 vs 0.284) and slalom progress collapsed (0.07 vs 0.135). Line-loss events stayed near 1 per run, so the wider array did not remove the loss. Mean rms_error is only about 0.02 while max_error reaches the 0.06 m off-track limit, so the robot tracks well on average and then fails in sudden bends. Higher kp (3.0 to 3.7) correlated with worse slalom and s-bend results, which points to overshoot at alternating bends rather than too little turn authority.

Changes. (1) kp 3.7 to 3.0, returning to the gain that performed best on the harder tracks. (2) kd 0.5 to 0.8, to damp the overshoot that the high kp was causing; steering oscillation on the oval was already 0.26 to 0.29, so this is a deliberate damping step and not a blind increase. (3) base_speed 1.4 to 1.3, to give the correction more time at sharp bends. The oval finish time (about 1.7 s) leaves enough margin that a small speed cut should not stop completion. (4) Keep the wide 16 mm array at x = -0.04 to 0.04 (spacing 0.02), so that coverage is not reduced, and keep ki 0.02, mass 0.6 kg, sensor y 0.03 m and last_direction line loss, so that only the gain, damping and speed move.

Expected result. Fewer off-track exits on the s-bend and slalom, with progress above 0.3 on the s-bend and above 0.2 on the slalom. Oval completion should hold at around 1 in 20 or better.

Hypotheses to test. (a) If max_error still reaches 0.06 on the slalom with kd 0.8, the limit is turn-in lag, so sensor y must move forward (toward 0.05) next. (b) If the robot becomes sluggish with progress stalled below 0.3 and no off-track exit, kd is too high and should drop to about 0.6. (c) If line_loss_events stay near 1 per run after the wider array, the loss is probably the terminal off-track event, so that metric should be ignored for array decisions.

Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort and noise_robustness, so that the damping effect can be separated from the speed effect.
